notes: §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR4: 'Its PICTURE character-string is restricted to certain combinations of the symbols 'A', 'X', '9', and the item is treated as if the character-string contained all 'X's. A PICTURE character-string which contains all 'A's or all '9's does not define an alphanumeric item'. AnalyzeCharacterString's A/X arm takes any string holding an A or an X whose symbols are all A, X or 9 and returns PicCategory.Alphanumeric with no EditMask and only a Length (CharacterPositions): nothing per position survives, so the item is the all-X item of that size at every edition, which is the 1985 treatment (2023 keeps '9' positions numeric; the compiler never did). All 'A' sets IsAlphabetic and all '9' falls to the numeric arm, so neither is alphanumeric; PictureComposition.Precedence admits A, X and 9 in any order and refuses any other symbol beside an A or X (COBOL1935). Probed at --std 85: PIC A9 holds '#?', PIC 9X holds 'ab', PIC 9A9 holds '*-+', a numeric integer moves to PIC A9A and both class tests compile on it; PIC XV9, XP, SX and AZ are refused. The witness stores '1A2B' in PIC A9XX and 'Z*' in PIC 9X.

next.reason: 1985: an alphanumeric PICTURE uses combinations of 'A', 'X', '9' 'and the item is treated as if the character-string contained all X's' (all-A and all-9 excluded); content any characters. §2023:13.18.40.4 GR6 accepts the same strings ('at least one symbol X, or at least two different symbols from this set'), but no 2023 rule treats the item as all X's: §2023:13.18.40.4 GR14 makes 'A' equivalent to 'X' only outside VALIDATE, and each '9' of a display item 'shall contain a numeric character in the range 0 through 9'. The content requirement for '9' positions in an alphanumeric item is stricter.
